_meta.what_this_is: A manifest of learning modules. Each carries a self-reported 'claimed_status' (what the author marked it: ready or draft) AND three checkable facts a reader can verify independently: sections_ok (all required sections present), self_test_passes (the module's --check ran green), recall_logged (a dated boss-fight recall pass exists). The point of the hub's whole doctrine: 'ready' is not something a module gets to declare -- it is DERIVED from the facts. A reader trusts the derived status, never the claimed one.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. Hand-authored so overclaims (marked ready, fails a criterion) and underclaims (marked draft, actually meets all) are exact and checkable.
_meta.format: required_criteria (all must hold for ready); modules [{id, claimed_status, sections_ok, self_test_passes, recall_logged}]
